title: The Long Way Round
gist_ar: حكاية حياة عن الفشل اللي طلع بداية.
text:
Nadia had been studying engineering for three years when she realised, quite suddenly, that she did not want it. She had grown up in a family with a background in medicine, which valued certainty, and at first she said nothing.

Meanwhile her results were getting worse. She had never struggled at anything before, and the experience frightened her more than the subject did. Eventually, in the middle of an examination she had not prepared for, she put down her pen and left. That was the first stage of something she could not yet describe.

Her father did not speak to her for a period of a month. Gradually, though, another event changed things: she began teaching mathematics to children in the neighbourhood, at first for nothing, then for a small fee. She had been doing it for a year before she understood that she had overcome the thing she had been afraid of.

When she finally graduated — from a different course, four years later than planned — she gave a short speech. She said she had spent a long time believing she had wasted three years. She had not wasted them. She had simply been taking the long way round, which, she added, is still a way to achieve something.

questions.q: What did she do during the examination?
options: She put down her pen and left
For nothing, then for a small fee
As a paid job at a school

questions.q: What does 'the long way round is still a way' imply?
options: A slower route is still a valid route
